A:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: classic tactical RPG art-direction sample A
Game art style approval study for revenge-memories, an original fantasy tactical RPG. Produce a landscape THREE-PANEL art sample, no text, no UI. Three equal vertical panels, separated by a small dark gutter. Target 1536x768.
CRITICAL STYLE: classic Fire Emblem Game Boy Advance tactical-map pixel art, restrained and charming 16-bit sprites, SOFT SIMPLE COLOR BLOCKS, a genuinely low native pixel density. The entire image should look like a NATIVE 384x192 pixel artwork enlarged exactly 4x with nearest neighbor. Each of three panels is a tiny native 128x192 environment, conceived as an 8 by 12 grid of 16x16 tiles. Broad flat shapes, clear clusters, 2–3 colors per material, no tiny decorative details. Muted outline colors rather than heavy black. The viewer must see large deliberate square pixels and simple economical sprites. This must NOT be a high-resolution painting disguised as pixel art.
Camera is the classic orthogonal top-down RPG tile-map view, with roofs visible and short front walls. No isometric projection, no perspective, no miniature model style, no high cliffs or dramatic realistic depth.
The three panels depict these same original story locations:
LEFT: snowy Western village. Three small simple timber cottages with muted blue/slate pitched roofs, snow caps, a few small fir-tree clusters, a small plain memorial stone, a winding dirt path partly surrounded by snow, a low rocky boundary. Buildings about 2 native tiles wide, individual trees about one tile. Show quiet human settlement, not lavish fantasy architecture.
MIDDLE: Strait harbor settlement. A small simple pale-stone gate and crenellated wall along the upper edge, three little low roof buildings, a small open courtyard containing a modest bronze sun-mirror tower on a stone pedestal, two timber docks and one small sailing boat in blue sea at the bottom. Architectural motifs are generic original fantasy; restrained gold sun/feather symbol only. No cross, torii, pagoda or ornate cathedral.
RIGHT: Eastern island ruined shrine and salt marsh. A broken pale-stone arch, two small broken columns and a low stepped sacred platform. Cream salt land in upper part, sparse green reeds and shallow teal water in lower part, simple natural shoreline curves built from obvious edge and corner tiles, a short plank walkway. The shrine has one tiny faded sun symbol.
Ground, paths, forest, walls and water remain easily distinguishable. Water is mostly flat blue with very few short simple pale ripple pixels, no complex caustics. Stone surfaces use large flat color regions, no individually rendered bricks. Fir-tree canopies are simple broad tiers, not thousands of needles. No grass microtexture, no clutter, no realistic shadows, no glossy highlights, no bloom, no 3D, no blur, no antialiased painted shading, no gradient, no grid lines, no characters or watermarks. This is style-only, NOT a deliverable tileset.
OPTION A — SOFT CLASSIC HANDHELD ADVENTURE.
Most directly evokes the warm, clear, modest tactical-map visual language of classic Fire Emblem GBA. Gentle medium-value colors, balanced daylight, grassy green, slightly desaturated cornflower blue sea, ivory stone, warm earth paths, slate blue roofs, pearl snow with lavender-blue shade. Simple softened silhouettes and low contrast within materials, enough contrast between walkable ground and obstacles. Mature fantasy adventure, warm and readable, not childish chibi. Use about 32 total colors. Keep visual density deliberately sparse.

Classic Super Famicom Fire Emblem map-sprite feeling, not modern detailed pixel illustration.
Re-render with large visibly square clusters as if the entire image were 384x192 native pixels. Flatten architecture into compact broad silhouettes. Roofs across all panels change to muted dusty PLUM/BROWN, with 2 flat color clusters and virtually no shingle lines. Stone walls and shrine change to SOFT ASH GRAY/LILAC, with 2–3 broad tones and at most a few coarse joint marks. Fir canopies and other foliage change to muted OLIVE/PINE, simplified into 3 broad layers; cliff ridges become short round gray rock bands, minimal rock faceting. Sea changes to desaturated GRAY BLUE, almost uniform with only tiny sparse pale wave strokes. Paths quiet taupe, snow pearl-gray with lavender shade, salt ground soft bone-gray. Sun relics dull aged brass with no gleam, no bloom. No contrasty black edging or sharp white highlights.
Remove approximately 70 percent of the existing tiny texture marks and decorative details, retaining all main objects and their legible silhouettes: 3 snow village cottages and memorial; harbor wall, houses, modest sun mirror, docks and sailboat; broken shrine, marsh shoreline and planks. Aim for 20–24 deliberate colors total. Soft palette but perfectly crisp low-resolution game pixels, NOT blur. Quiet mature grief and old faith. No additional objects, labels, UI, characters or modern polished miniature detailing.

OPTION C — WARM SOFT CLASSICAL FANTASY.
A distinct softer alternative within the classic Fire Emblem / 16-bit tactical RPG family. Warm mellow sunlit palette: pale buttercream stone, ochre and peach earth, muted terracotta roofs, moss and celadon foliage, gentle aquamarine sea, cream snow with soft blue-lavender shaded clusters. Absolutely no glossy modern rendering.
Change shape design from the sharper blue-roof version: houses are low and broad with simpler slightly rounded roof silhouettes, three-tone roof clusters without visible individual roof shingles; firs have broad gently tapering layers, broadleaf canopies use rounded 3-tone clusters; cliffs are low rounded tan rock bands, not dramatic jagged peaks; harbor fort and ruined shrine use thick slightly rounded stone masses with almost no brick detail. Contours should be SOFT COLORED PIXEL EDGES, not heavy black outlines. Snow shore and sand transitions use simple warm-edged chunky stepping patterns. A small bronze mirror sun tower, original faded sun motif in eastern ruins; keep the visual design restrained.
About 32–40 carefully harmonious colors. Large calm flat ground areas with sparse single-cluster grass flowers and stone markings. Softness comes from palette and shape design, NOT blur or anti-aliasing. Genuine economical low-resolution pixel sprites drawn on an orthogonal tile grid. Mood: an old world capable of tenderness and grief, faith turning into control, warmth that makes the later losses matter. Not toy-like, not chibi, not cute fairytale caricature.
Keep the three scene panels matched to options A/B in content and scale. LEFT three snow village cottages and plain memorial; MIDDLE small walled harbor, sun mirror, docks and small boat; RIGHT broken sun shrine, salt ground and marsh reeds. No people, text or UI.
rejected_modern_draft:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: game pixel-art direction comparison, option A
Create a LANDSCAPE 3-panel PIXEL ART style study for the fantasy tactical RPG revenge-memories. This is a visual art-direction sample, NOT a finished tileset or a big illustrated world map. Target 1536x768, three equally wide vertical panels with a narrow dark gutter between them. No text anywhere.
All three panels must be TRUE 2D overhead orthogonal-grid RPG game environments, viewed from the north with short front facades on buildings, NO isometric diamond grid, NO perspective horizon, NO miniature model or cinematic 3D rendering. Terrain should clearly suggest reusable square game tiles at a coherent pixel density: broad readable pixel clusters, clean silhouettes, modest detail, native 32px terrain-tile craft enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Do not draw grid lines. Lighting from upper left throughout. No blur, gradients, depth-of-field, anti-aliased painting, noisy procedural textures or UI.
The same exact environments and content appear in every style option:
LEFT PANEL — Western snow village, the home of the teenage hero Hunahpu. Three modest timber-and-stone cottages, snow-covered pitched roofs, a tiny plain memorial stone at the edge of the hamlet, snowy fir forest, rocky ridge along the upper-left, a clear snow-to-earth path connecting the cottages, a small patch of thawing grass. The story has loss and displacement: dignified, lived-in, no cheerful toy-town decoration.
MIDDLE PANEL — Strait harbor city where the victory ceremony and reunion occur. A weathered sandstone gatehouse and compact walled coastal settlement in the upper half, small timber docks projecting into the lower-half sea, one simple wooden sailboat, clearly legible dirt/stone paths. At the central plaza stands a slender stone sunlight-relay tower with a bronze-gold round mirror and a restrained seven-feather sun symbol. This church has genuinely helped people and is also becoming controlling: beauty and authority both visible. No Christian crosses, European cathedral spires, Japanese torii, contemporary buildings, guns or engines.
RIGHT PANEL — Eastern islands' ancient sunken sanctuary adjoining pale salt land. A broken pale stone arch and a short weathered stepped ritual platform with one faded gold sun emblem in the upper-middle. Salt-white/sandy ground above, jade tidal reeds and shallow blue water below, irregular rocky shore, a short complete plank crossing. Show the large fracture's physical cost through broken stairs and partially submerged foundations. The game is original fantasy with a few feather/sun motifs, not a reconstruction of a real culture.
No characters, battle effects, labels, numbered tiles, border decoration or watermarks. Keep navigable ground visually distinct from forest, cliffs and water. Buildings and trees should read as modular assets, NOT large photo-real terrain masses. Each panel fills its area, including ground to its edges.
STYLE OPTION A — CLEAR CLASSIC ADVENTURE.
Polished modern 16-bit pixel art with disciplined 32px-tile readability. Restrained 48–64 color palette, small crisp square clusters, 3 distinct tones per material, flat coherent shape design, a subtle dark outline only where object silhouettes need separation. Western roofs are muted brick red; pine foliage emerald; snow pearl white with cool pale-blue shade. Harbor has warm pale sandstone, rust-red timber roofs and bronze sunlight machinery; sea luminous but restrained turquoise. Eastern ruin stone is warm ivory, reeds jade, salt light cream. Balanced daylight with very clean ground/object separation, readable at mobile display size. Mature adventure mood, neither childish chibi nor grim horror. Compared with other options, this style has the strongest geometric clarity, lighter detail density and the most obvious tile-friendly production language.
